what.a: Open this computer's terminals from your phone or any browser: see how Claude Code or Codex is doing and reply to keep it going; run commands and read logs too. Close the page and tasks keep running.

vs.q: Is it like remote control tools such as ToDesk?
vs.a: No. ToDesk streams the whole desktop, which suits graphical apps; Looklook opens only the terminal, built for the command line and AI coding assistants.

better.q: How is it better than remote desktop?
better.a: Text is sharp on a phone and typing works normally, with an Esc/Ctrl key bar. Only text is sent, so it uses little data and stays smooth on poor signal; the computer can be locked, and servers and NAS work too. For graphical desktop work, remote desktop is the better fit.

install.q: Do I install it on both the computer and phone?
install.a: Only this computer needs Looklook (the one you're using now). Phones and other computers need nothing: open your personal address in a browser and sign in.

safety.title: Security notice
safety.body: The Looklook dashboard uses port {{port}} on this computer. If this computer has a public IP (e.g. a cloud server), do not open port {{port}} to the internet in the firewall, security group or router. To connect from outside, use your personal address (requires signing in to Looklook).

access.title: Access control
access.intro: This computer can always open the dashboard itself. Here you decide whether other devices can connect directly to it. To use it from your phone outside, use your personal address; no change is needed here.
access.lan: Allow devices on the LAN to open it
access.lan_hint: When on, phones and computers on the same Wi‑Fi or router can open the dashboard by entering this computer's LAN address (e.g. http://192.168.1.20:1234) in a browser. Useful when Looklook runs on a NAS or another computer at home. Don't enable it on shared networks such as cafés or offices. If unsure, leave it off.
access.lan_urls: Devices on the LAN open this address:
access.lan_unknown: Couldn't find this computer's LAN address. Check its IP in your router's admin page, then open http://that-IP:{{port}}/
access.lan_no_code: Also enable the access code, otherwise anyone on the same Wi‑Fi can open your terminals.
access.code_hint: The access code is stored only on this computer (in Looklook's local database) and is never uploaded to the Looklook server. When on, devices on the LAN or allowlist must enter it the first time they open the dashboard, and that browser remembers it for 30 days; this computer itself doesn't need it. Purpose: stop other people on the same network from opening your terminals.
access.code_forgot: After changing the code, browsers that entered the old one must enter it again. Forgot it? Open this page on this computer to view it, or run looklook access in a terminal. 10 wrong attempts lock you out for 15 minutes.
access.list_hint: Usually not needed. Add one only to open the dashboard directly from a fixed public IP (e.g. an office network); enter a single IP or a range such as 203.0.113.7 or 203.0.113.0/24. Enabling the access code is recommended when using the allowlist.
access.list_no_code: IPs on the allowlist can currently open the dashboard without an access code; enabling the access code is recommended.
access.open_host_hint: The address Looklook opens in the browser at startup. If Looklook runs on a NAS or server and you usually open it from another computer on the LAN, enter that machine's IP or domain; host only, without http:// or a port. When using a domain, that domain is also allowed. Leave empty for this computer.
access.remote_only: Access control can't be changed when opened through the personal address. Change it on this computer or on an allowed LAN device.
access.fw_title: Windows showed "Windows Defender Firewall has blocked some features of this app"?
access.fw_why: The Looklook dashboard listens on all network adapters so you can allow LAN access when needed, so Windows asks on first run whether to allow it. This isn't a virus warning; choose according to how you use it:
access.fw_local: Only using it on this computer: click "Cancel". This computer opens it as usual, and using your personal address from your phone outside is unaffected.
access.fw_lan: To let other devices at home open it: tick only "Private networks" and click "Allow access". Don't tick "Public networks" (cafés, airports, etc.).
access.fw_profile: Allowed but still can't connect: in Windows Settings → Network & Internet → Wi‑Fi (or Ethernet) → your network, set the network profile type to "Private".
access.fw_fix: Clicked the wrong option and want to change it: open Control Panel → Windows Defender Firewall → Allow an app through Windows Firewall → Change settings, find looklook and tick only "Private". You can also run this in PowerShell as administrator:
access.fw_never: To never see this prompt: set the environment variable LOOKLOOK_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:1234 and reopen Looklook. Then the dashboard can only be opened on this computer, and LAN access won't work.
access.lan_switch: Offer the local network when opened remotely
access.lan_switch_hint: When you open Looklook remotely with your account while on the same network as this computer (say, your phone at home), the page offers a faster direct connection over the local network. Only browsers signed in to your account can switch; it doesn't need "Allow LAN" above or the access code.

reason.dns: Can't find the Looklook server's address (DNS lookup failed). Check this computer's network, or switch DNS (e.g. 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1).

reason.timeout: Connecting to the server timed out. Check that your network works; office or school networks sometimes block this kind of connection, so try a phone hotspot.
reason.network: The network is unreachable. Make sure this computer is connected to the internet.

reason.handshake: The encrypted handshake with the server failed. Usually the network is interfering, or Looklook is too old — please update to the latest version.
reason.heartbeat: The connection to the server dropped (no response for a long time). Reconnecting automatically.
reason.config: Couldn't write the remote access configuration. Check disk space and file permissions.
reason.other: Something went wrong connecting to the server; Looklook will retry. If it keeps failing, expand the technical details and send them to us.

guide.s3: Want to continue on your phone? Open the personal address at the top of the page and sign in to the same account.

relays.title: Remote route
relays.intro: When you open this computer from your phone or another computer, the data goes through a Looklook route. Looklook tests the routes regularly and uses the one with the lowest latency, so you usually don't need to do anything.
relays.when_slow: If remote access feels laggy or typing is delayed, pick a route with lower latency below. Once you pick one yourself it won't switch automatically, and Looklook remembers your choice. If a route gets noticeably slow, you'll see a reminder at the top of the page.

relays.switch_note: Switching routes disconnects any open remote pages for a few seconds, then they reconnect on their own. Your personal address stays the same.
